work.title: Cello Concerto in E minor
work.movement: Abridged complete concerto, including shortened finale

version.value: Four acoustic sides: one abridged movement per side.
version.note: This is the abridged whole concerto, not the complete score or a sixteen-minute finale. The supplied stream already joins all four sides. Only a continuous early finale passage is aligned with the complete Skidmore finale; neither complete work durations nor omitted music are equated. The exact cuts and acoustic-session instrumental substitutions are not established, so no modern-score orchestra timeline is projected onto this recording.

performers.note: The archive quotes Moore on the ensemble’s New Symphony/Royal Albert Hall identity; the published credit follows the photographed labels rather than silently expanding their wording.

date.note: The later session applies to replacement side three, HO 4607-AF. The finale, HO 4198-AF, belongs to the December 1919 session; the listen ID names the two-session recording rather than dating every side to 1920.

place.note: Source-reported session location, not inferred from the record manufacturer’s address.

label.value: His Master’s Voice / The Gramophone Company

catalogue.note: The archive dates first issue to May 1921 for D541 and June 1921 for D545.

matrixTakeSides.note: The archive says take numbers are not indicated on the discs. It reports take 2 for side three and an additional take-2 attribution for side one from Moore; no take is assigned here to the finale.

credits.note: No transfer engineer is identified; an uploader is not automatically the engineer.

date.note: No transfer date is established; upload dates are not used as transfer dates.

processing.value: Single supplied FLAC with MP3 derivative; archive reports a digital pitch adjustment to side three.
processing.note: The archive estimates A=435 Hz at 78 rpm for the earlier sides and A=430 Hz for side three before correction. This is not a verified original session tuning. No local concatenation or audio processing was performed.

digital.format: Internet Archive VBR MP3 derivative of the single supplied 24-bit FLAC

composition.value: Underlying Elgar composition is out of copyright under the ordinary life-plus-70 term.
composition.note: The archive identifies Elgar’s dates as 1857–1934. This term calculation does not clear a later edition.

recording.value: United States public domain: recording first issued in 1921, before the 1926 cutoff.
recording.note: Programme rule 2. The item states May and June 1921 issues and cites contemporary reviews; its metadata and description contain no non-commercial licence. The eligibility is based on the issued sound recording, not the composition. No unrestricted modern restoration licence is invented.

rights.creditLine: Edward Elgar, Cello Concerto, Op. 85, abridged acoustic recording; Beatrice Harrison, cello; Symphony Orchestra; Edward Elgar, conductor. HMV D541 and D545, issued 1921; single Internet Archive transfer.
